title: Australia pricing strategy meeting
zhtitle: 澳洲经销商价格策略会谈
intro: 与澳洲经销商讨论销量下滑和价格竞争：大项目联合定价、小单流失、沟通机制和库存补差。
note: 根据会议英文转写整理，措辞有精简；具体价格、公司名和人名已隐去。音频为 AI 合成语音。

lines.en: It would be helpful to review pricing across the board, especially for larger projects. We want to be fair and [[transparent]] wherever possible.
lines.zh: 全面审视一下价格会很有帮助，尤其是大项目。我们希望尽可能公平、透明。

lines.en: We should avoid simply saying that our price is fixed and nothing can be done.
lines.zh: 我们不应该只是说价格是固定的、没得商量。

lines.en: Over time, [[competitors]] may take over the relationships we have built by offering a lower price and approaching our customers directly.
lines.zh: 时间久了，竞争对手可能会报更低的价、直接找我们的客户，把我们建立的客户关系抢走。

lines.en: Instead, we should be prepared to compete on selected jobs, so that we can keep our relationships and help [[stabilize]] market pricing.
lines.zh: 相反，我们应该准备好在部分项目上去竞争，这样才能保住客户关系，也有助于稳定市场价格。

lines.en: Installers and builders often look at price first. It may take five or ten years for them to realize that a cheaper product is of lower [[quality]].
lines.zh: 安装商和建筑商往往先看价格。他们可能要五到十年才会发现便宜的产品质量更差。

lines.en: There are cases where we win despite being more expensive, but there are also cases where we simply lose the project. That is becoming quite common.
lines.zh: 有时候我们贵也能拿下，但也有时候直接丢了项目。现在这种情况越来越常见。

lines.en: It would be a waste of time to keep a [[fixed price]] for several months and only then discover that it is not working.
lines.zh: 如果固定一个价格好几个月，最后才发现行不通，那就是浪费时间。

lines.en: My colleague explained that closer [[cooperation]] would benefit both companies.
lines.zh: 我同事解释说，更紧密的合作对双方都有好处。

lines.en: The aim is to reduce costs in a fair and open way, rather than one side hiding costs or keeping the remaining [[margin]] for itself.
lines.zh: 目的是用公平、公开的方式降低成本，而不是一方隐藏成本或把剩下的利润留给自己。

lines.en: For example, if a special project of around five thousand square metres comes up, the customer could ask for our [[support]] on price.
lines.zh: 比如，如果出现一个五千平方米左右的特殊项目，客户可以请我们在价格上给予支持。

lines.en: Prices for core products and [[regular orders]] could stay at the current level.
lines.zh: 核心产品和常规订单的价格可以保持现有水平。

lines.en: For special projects, however, the teams should discuss a [[project-specific]] reduction to improve the chance of winning.
lines.zh: 但对于特殊项目，双方团队应该商量针对单个项目的降价，提高中标的机会。

lines.en: Smaller projects are also being lost. The customer may think the price is too high and the order is too small to ask for a [[discount]].
lines.zh: 小项目也在流失。客户可能觉得价格太高、订单又太小，不好意思要折扣。

lines.en: So the customer never asks, and the project is lost without us even knowing that price was the reason.
lines.zh: 所以客户根本不来问，项目丢了，我们甚至不知道是价格的原因。

lines.en: Since our [[sales volume]] has been declining, we certainly want to win more of the large-project opportunities.
lines.zh: 既然我们的销量一直在下滑，我们当然想多拿一些大项目机会。

lines.en: However, this cannot be achieved by us alone. We may need to work with our entire [[supply network]] for that particular project.
lines.zh: 但这不是我们一家能做到的。针对那个项目，我们可能需要整个供应链一起支持。

lines.en: A customer may take only a few hundred square metres from [[stock]] each month, but several such orders can add up to thousands of square metres.
lines.zh: 一个客户每个月可能只从库存拿几百平方米，但好几个这样的订单加起来就是几千平方米。

sections.name: A faster channel for market information

lines.en: My plan is to discuss with our suppliers how we can provide regular pricing support for small and [[medium-sized]] projects.
lines.zh: 我的计划是和我们的供应商商量，怎样给中小项目提供常规的价格支持。

lines.en: For large projects, we should establish a separate [[communication channel]].
lines.zh: 大项目方面，我们应该建立一个单独的沟通渠道。

lines.en: Your product manager and purchasing manager could tell us directly how much support is needed and what competitors are offering.
lines.zh: 你们的产品经理和采购经理可以直接告诉我们需要多少支持、竞争对手报的是什么条件。

lines.en: Order volumes have been declining for about a year. Once [[market share]] has been lost to competitors, winning it back can be difficult.
lines.zh: 订单量已经下滑了大约一年。市场份额一旦被竞争对手拿走，再抢回来就难了。

lines.en: If we had known earlier, we could have responded quickly and kept strong relationships with installers and [[designers]].
lines.zh: 如果我们早点知道，就能快速反应，和安装商、设计师保持牢固的关系。

lines.en: I will update the [[pricing structure]] as soon as possible this week, by Wednesday.
lines.zh: 我会在这周尽快更新价格体系，周三之前。

sections.name: Reviewing the pipeline and sharing margins
sections.zhname: 梳理在跟项目、共担利润

lines.en: Going forward, we should pull together all projects in the [[pipeline]], including those being quoted, and segment them by project size.
lines.zh: 接下来，我们要把所有在跟的项目汇总起来，包括正在报价的，按项目大小分类。

lines.en: For each category, we should communicate with you more frequently and discuss how we can compete more [[aggressively]].
lines.zh: 每一类我们都应该和你们更频繁地沟通，讨论怎样更积极地去竞争。

lines.en: If a competitor offers a lower price, we should discuss whether we can [[match]] it.
lines.zh: 如果竞争对手报了更低的价，我们应该讨论能不能跟上。

lines.en: This does not mean asking you to absorb the entire discount. Both sides should share the impact on [[margins]].
lines.zh: 这不是要你们承担全部折扣，双方应该共同分担利润上的影响。

lines.en: We may have to accept a lower margin on that particular project, but at least we would have a chance to [[retain]] the market share.
lines.zh: 在那个项目上我们可能得接受更低的利润，但至少有机会保住市场份额。

lines.en: I think this is the right approach. First, I look forward to receiving an email with the relevant information.
lines.zh: 我觉得这个方向是对的。第一，我等着收到包含相关信息的邮件。

lines.en: Second, we already hold [[quarterly meetings]]. I would like to invite someone from the sales team to join them.
lines.zh: 第二，我们本来就有季度会议，我想邀请销售团队的人也一起参加。

lines.en: We should be able to [[extract]] the project and colour information from the system by the end of this week.
lines.zh: 我们应该能在这周末前从系统里导出项目和颜色信息。

lines.en: We could catch up once a month, or communicate by email whenever something [[urgent]] comes up.
lines.zh: 我们可以每月碰一次，或者有急事的时候发邮件沟通。

lines.en: Instead of acting only as supplier and customer, we should work together to compete for these projects.
lines.zh: 我们不应该只是供应商和客户的关系，而应该一起去争取这些项目。

lines.en: Most of the products we sell are probably already in stock. Perhaps you could provide some [[credit]] on future orders to help us compete.
lines.zh: 我们卖的大部分产品可能都已经在库存里了。也许你们可以在以后的订单上给一些抵扣，帮我们去竞争。

lines.en: For example, if a project requires five thousand square metres and we have stock available, we would like to be able to sell it.
lines.zh: 比如一个项目需要五千平方米，而我们有现货，我们希望能把它卖出去。

lines.en: If we are competing for rail projects and already have several thousand square metres in stock, we want to make sure we are [[aligned]] first.
lines.zh: 如果我们在争取铁路项目、手上已经有几千平方米库存，我们想先确保双方意见一致。

lines.en: Could you clarify what you mean by a credit? Do you mean that you need more time to pay?
lines.zh: 能解释一下你说的抵扣是什么意思吗？是指需要更长的付款时间吗？

lines.en: Let me explain. Say we have a project for three thousand square metres in a [[standard colour]] and want to compete by reducing the price.
lines.zh: 我解释一下。假设有个三千平方米的标准色项目，我们想通过降价去竞争。

lines.en: Both of our margins will be lower. And the stock in our [[warehouse]] was already bought at the old, higher price.
lines.zh: 我们双方的利润都会变低。而且我们仓库里的库存是之前按更高的价格买的。

lines.en: So if you agree to lower the price for this project, we are asking for a credit for the [[difference]] on that stock.
lines.zh: 所以如果你们同意给这个项目降价，我们希望库存那部分的差价能给我们抵扣。

lines.en: Yes, I understand. It is similar to a credit against stock already held, to be used on the [[next order]].
lines.zh: 明白了。就类似于对已有库存给一个抵扣，用在下一个订单上。

lines.en: We would only offer that project price after confirming that you agree. We would not compete aggressively without first aligning with you.
lines.zh: 我们只会在确认你们同意之后才报那个项目价。不会在没和你们对齐之前就去压价竞争。

lines.en: He means that when a special project comes up, the teams can discuss a [[temporary]], project-specific arrangement.
lines.zh: 他的意思是，遇到特殊项目时，双方可以商量一个临时的、只针对这个项目的安排。

lines.en: Communication is probably the most important part of this process.
lines.zh: 沟通可能是这里面最重要的。

lines.en: Most of our competitors also [[purchase]] from China, so under comparable conditions we should have certain advantages.
lines.zh: 我们大多数竞争对手也是从中国采购，所以同等条件下我们应该有一定优势。

lines.en: Some competitors are smaller companies where the CEO handles both sales and purchasing, which makes them more [[flexible]].
lines.zh: 有些竞争对手是小公司，CEO 同时管销售和采购，所以更灵活。

lines.en: Losing a project without making any effort to win it is a waste of an opportunity. Winning it together would benefit both sides.
lines.zh: 不做任何努力就丢掉项目是浪费机会。一起拿下订单对双方都有好处。

lines.en: Will you still review the [[base pricing]], or are we only looking at large projects? I just want to make sure I understand.
lines.zh: 你们还会审核基础价格吗，还是只看大项目？我只是想确认我理解对了。

lines.en: We will review both. I will prepare the pricing information and send it to you this week.
lines.zh: 两个都会看。我会准备好价格资料，这周发给你们。

sections.name: Closing: flexibility and regular reviews
sections.zhname: 结尾：灵活定价与定期复盘

lines.en: Thank you for being [[open-minded]]. Competing for large building projects is challenging, and we need flexibility in pricing and service.
lines.zh: 感谢你们的开放态度。争取大型建筑项目很难，我们在价格和服务上都需要灵活。

lines.en: We can take care of the service side, but pricing is more difficult.
lines.zh: 服务这边我们能搞定，但价格更难。

lines.en: Once you update the pricing, we will review the projects and gather information about competitors: where they [[source]] their products, what quality they offer, and what prices they can reach.
lines.zh: 你们更新价格后，我们会梳理项目，收集竞争对手的信息：他们从哪里进货、质量怎样、能报到什么价。

lines.en: I think we should meet at least once a month or once every two months to review pricing and trading strategies.
lines.zh: 我觉得我们至少每月或每两个月见一次，复盘价格和贸易策略。

lines.en: Very good. I completely agree.
lines.zh: 很好，我完全同意。

lines.en: Thank you very much. We appreciate your time.
lines.zh: 非常感谢，感谢大家抽出时间。

quiz.q: According to Richard, how long might it take installers to notice that a cheaper product is lower quality?
quiz.explain: 安装商和建筑商往往先看价格，可能要五到十年才发现便宜产品质量差。

quiz.q: Why are small orders being lost without anyone noticing?
options: The products are out of stock
Customers think the order is too small to ask for a discount
quiz.explain: 客户觉得价格高、单子又小，不好意思问折扣，项目就悄悄丢了。

quiz.q: How long have order volumes been declining?
quiz.explain: 订单量下滑了大约一年才被发现。

quiz.q: By when will Flora update the pricing structure?
options: By the end of the month
quiz.explain: 她说这周尽快更新价格体系，周三之前。

quiz.q: What does Richard suggest for competing on special projects?
options: The supplier absorbs the whole discount
Both sides share the impact on margins
The distributor absorbs the whole discount
quiz.explain: 不是让一方承担全部折扣，而是双方共担利润影响。

quiz.q: Who will Flora invite to join the existing quarterly meetings?
quiz.explain: 邀请销售团队的人参加季度会议，及时了解市场。

quiz.q: What does 'credit' mean in Richard's proposal?
options: Compensation for the price difference on stock already bought at a higher price
quiz.explain: 不是延长账期，而是对按旧价买进的库存给差价抵扣，用在下一个订单上。

quiz.q: Why can some smaller competitors react more flexibly?
options: Their CEO handles both sales and purchasing
quiz.explain: 小公司 CEO 同时管销售和采购，决策更快。

quiz.q: How often does Richard suggest meeting to review pricing?
options: Once a month or every two months
Only when there is a problem
quiz.explain: 至少每月或每两个月见一次，复盘价格和贸易策略。

items.zh: 在跟项目 / 项目储备
